issues.main_description_html:
[Tour Detail] Integrate Upload Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN uploads finished tours to GoThru via /streeteditor/upload-tour (apil.gothru.co); see docs/analyze.md §2.7, §3.4, and the upload-reliability notes in §5.

Goal

Implement "Upload Tour" in the Flutter app: send a local tour (project + panoramas + connections + levels) to GoThru, with progress, pre-checks, and clear success/failure handling.

Scope

  • Pre-upload checks: connectivity, storage/quota, per-panorama GoThru existence (skip already-present panoramas).
  • Upload project metadata, panorama assets, connections, and levels.
  • Progress feedback (per-panorama / overall); update local uploaded / virtual_tour_status.
  • Surface errors with retry; no silent failure.

Out of Scope

  • Retry-condition fix specifics (tracked in the RN repo); moderation; Google publishing.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Upload sends the full tour and reflects true server state on completion (uploaded/virtual_tour_status).
  • Pre-checks (network, storage, per-panorama existence) run before/within upload.
  • Progress shown; already-uploaded panoramas are skipped (no duplicates).
  • Errors surfaced with retry; partial uploads are resumable/clean.
  • Works with the signed-in session token.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Upload a tour (happy path)

  1. Open a complete local tour → Upload.
  2. Expected: Upload completes; tour marked uploaded; appears correctly on GoThru.

TC-2 — Skip already-uploaded panoramas

  1. Upload a tour where some panoramas already exist on GoThru.
  2. Expected: Only missing panoramas are sent; no duplicates server-side.

TC-3 — Offline / no connection

  1. Attempt upload offline.
  2. Expected: Clear "no internet" message; upload not started.

TC-4 — Quota / storage exceeded

  1. Upload when over quota.
  2. Expected: Clear error; no broken partial state looping.

TC-5 — Interruption + retry

  1. Interrupt mid-upload, then retry.
  2. Expected: Resumes remaining work; completes; one tour, no duplicates.

TC-6 — Progress feedback

  1. Upload a large tour.
  2. Expected: Visible progress; UI not frozen.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: local tour data intact whether upload succeeds or fails.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED — real-data mobile validation found an upload-blocking coding defect. The upload did not complete; unexecuted scenarios are not marked as passed.

ID Method Scenario Result Status
TC-1 Gray Box Upload a complete local tour Upload failed during the prepare connections stage with HTTP 409: level already exist FAIL — Bug
TC-2 Gray Box Skip already-uploaded panoramas Not executed because the upload was blocked before completion Not executed
TC-3 Black Box Attempt upload while offline Not executed in this run Not executed
TC-4 Black Box Upload while quota or storage is exceeded Not executed; no safe quota-exceeded QA condition was used Not executed
TC-5 Gray / Black Box Interrupt an upload and retry Not executed because the initial upload was blocked Not executed
TC-6 White / Gray Box Verify progress on a large upload The upload reached preparation but could not proceed past the failing connection preparation step Blocked by bug
Regression Gray Box Verify local tour data after failed upload Requires final device confirmation after the failed attempt; not asserted as passed in this run Not executed

Confirmed Coding Bug

Severity Actual result Expected result Impact
High Upload Tour fails at prepare connections with HTTP 409 level already exist. The upload must prepare and upload the tour's connections and levels without rejecting a valid existing level, or it must handle an already-existing level idempotently. A tour containing the affected level/connection state cannot be uploaded to GoThru.

Code Review Summary

Area Reviewed behavior Result
Upload pre-processing Connection preparation reached the server but received a 409 conflict for an existing level FAIL — Bug
Error visibility The HTTP 409 failure was surfaced to the tester PASS
End-to-end upload completion Cannot complete while the level conflict occurs FAIL — Blocked by bug
Remaining upload behavior Not evaluated after the blocking failure Not executed

Validation Results

Tested condition Application result Status
Upload a complete tour with connections and levels prepare connections failed: level already exist (HTTP 409) Fail
Server conflict is visible to the user The failure message was shown Pass
Upload completes and reflects final server state Blocked by the HTTP 409 defect Not executed

[Tour Detail] Integrate Save Images (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN saves panorama images to the device gallery via expo-media-library (see docs/analyze.md §2.1, §2.7 and app permissions). Flutter equivalent uses a gallery-save plugin with proper permissions.

Goal

Implement "Save Images" in Tour Detail: export a tour's panorama image(s) from local storage to the device's photo gallery, with permission handling.

Scope

  • Save one or all panoramas of a tour to the device gallery.
  • Request/handle photo-library save permission (Android/iOS).
  • Progress + success/failure feedback; saved images use the original/full-resolution file.

Out of Scope

  • Editing images; uploading; sharing to third-party apps.

Acceptance Criteria

  • User can save a panorama (or all) to the device gallery.
  • Save permission requested/handled correctly on both platforms.
  • Saved files are the full-resolution panorama images.
  • Progress + result feedback; errors surfaced (no silent failure).

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Save a single image (happy path)

  1. Open a tour → select a panorama → Save Image.
  2. Expected: Image appears in the device gallery; success confirmation.

TC-2 — Save all images

  1. Choose Save All for a tour with several panoramas.
  2. Expected: All images saved; progress shown; count matches.

TC-3 — Permission denied

  1. Deny photo-save permission, then try saving.
  2. Expected: Clear guidance to enable permission; no crash.

TC-4 — Resolution check

  1. Inspect a saved image.
  2. Expected: It's the original/full-resolution panorama (not a thumbnail).

TC-5 — Offline

  1. Save while offline.
  2. Expected: Works (local operation); no network dependency.

TC-6 — Large batch

  1. Save all for a tour with many panoramas.
  2. Expected: Completes without freezing; all saved.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: saving does not modify or move the app's local panorama files.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: PASS — real-device mobile validation was completed by the QA tester using real tour data. No coding bug was confirmed.

[Connection] Integrate List Panorama Not Connected (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: Within the add-connection flow, the app shows panoramas that have no connection yet, so the user knows what still needs linking; see docs/analyze.md §2.2 and §3.3 (panoramas, connections).

Goal

Implement a "Not Connected" panorama list in the Flutter app: show the project's panoramas that are not yet part of any connection, as a guide for completing the tour graph.

Scope

  • Query panoramas for the project that do not appear as main_id or link_id in any connections row.
  • Render them as a list/grid with thumbnails.
  • Update live as connections are added/removed.
  • Empty state when all panoramas are connected.

Out of Scope

  • The add/remove connection actions themselves (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • List shows exactly the panoramas with no connections.
  • Updates immediately when a connection is added/removed.
  • Empty state shown when everything is connected.
  • Works offline; renders from local DB.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Shows unconnected panoramas (happy path)

  1. Open a tour with some connected and some unconnected panoramas.
  2. Expected: Only the unconnected ones are listed.

TC-2 — Updates after connecting

  1. Connect one of the listed panoramas.
  2. Expected: It disappears from the not-connected list.

TC-3 — Updates after removing a connection

  1. Remove a connection so a panorama becomes unconnected.
  2. Expected: It appears in the not-connected list.

TC-4 — Empty state

  1. Connect all panoramas.
  2. Expected: Not-connected list shows an empty state.

TC-5 — Offline / persistence

  1. View offline; relaunch and reopen.
  2. Expected: Correct list from local DB; consistent after restart.

TC-6 — Accuracy

  1. Cross-check against the connections data.
  2. Expected: List matches panoramas truly absent from connections.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: listing does not modify connection/panorama data.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: PASS — real-device mobile validation was completed with real tour data. No coding bug was confirmed.

TC-3 Gray Box Remove a connection Previously connected panorama became eligible and appeared in the candidate list TP PASS
TC-4 Black Box All panoramas connected Empty state displayed; no crash TN PASS
TC-5 Black Box Offline relaunch and reopen Candidate list remained correct from local data TP PASS
TC-6 Gray Box Cross-check candidates against connection data Unconnected panoramas appeared; connected panoramas did not appear as candidates TP + TN PASS
Regression Black Box Cancel/back before saving a connection No panorama or connection data changed TN PASS

[Moderation] Integrate Delete Moderation (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN moderation flow (src/pages/moderation); projects reference a moderation record via moderation_id (docs/analyze.md §2.6, §3.3).

Goal

Implement "Delete Moderation" in the Flutter app: remove a project's moderation record and clear its link (moderation_id), with confirmation.

Scope

  • Delete action for a project's moderation record (with confirm).
  • Remove the record via the GoThru API and/or local state; clear moderation_id on the project.
  • Success/failure feedback; UI reflects the cleared state.

Out of Scope

  • Save moderation (separate task); deleting the project itself.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Delete prompts for confirmation.
  • On confirm: moderation record removed and moderation_id cleared on the project.
  • Cancel leaves moderation intact.
  • Errors surfaced; state persists after restart.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Delete moderation (happy path)

  1. Open a project with moderation → Delete Moderation → confirm.
  2. Expected: Record removed; project no longer linked (moderation_id cleared).

TC-2 — Cancel

  1. Trigger delete, then cancel.
  2. Expected: Moderation remains.

TC-3 — Network error

  1. Delete while offline / simulate API failure.
  2. Expected: Clear error; retry possible; no half-deleted state.

TC-4 — Persistence

  1. Delete, relaunch, reopen.
  2. Expected: Moderation stays removed.

TC-5 — Project intact

  1. After deleting moderation, check the project.
  2. Expected: Project, panoramas, connections, levels unaffected.

TC-6 — Re-save after delete

  1. Delete moderation, then save a new one.
  2. Expected: New record creates and links cleanly.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: deleting moderation does not delete or modify tour content.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED — real-device mobile validation with real data found one coding defect. All other validated scenarios passed.

ID Method Scenario Real-device result Status
TC-1 White / Gray Box Delete moderation while online and confirm Moderation was deleted and the UI reflected the cleared state PASS
TC-2 Black Box Cancel deletion Moderation remained intact PASS
TC-3 Black Box Delete moderation while offline Moderation was deleted without an error message FAIL — Bug
TC-4 Gray Box Relaunch after deletion Deleted moderation state persisted after restart PASS
TC-5 Gray Box Verify project content after deletion Project, panoramas, connections, and levels remained intact PASS
TC-6 Gray Box Save moderation again after deletion New moderation could be saved and linked cleanly PASS

Confirmed Coding Bug

Severity Actual result Expected result Impact
High With no internet, confirming Delete Moderation removed moderation without showing an error. Offline/API failure must show a clear error, allow retry, and leave no half-deleted state. A user can believe the server-side moderation deletion succeeded although the operation was performed offline; the failure is silent.

Code Review Summary

Area Reviewed behavior Result
Confirmation flow User is prompted before the destructive action PASS
Success and persistence Confirmed deletion updates the visible state and remains removed after restart PASS
Offline/API failure handling No error was surfaced; deletion proceeded while offline FAIL — Bug
Project-data safety Tour project, panoramas, connections, and levels remained unchanged PASS
Re-save flow A new moderation can be created after deletion PASS

Validation Results

Tested condition Application result Status
Online deletion confirmed Moderation was deleted and the state persisted Pass
User cancels deletion Moderation remained intact Pass
No internet connection Moderation was deleted without an error Fail
After restart The deleted state remained consistent Pass

Evidence type: real-device mobile validation with real data, reported by QA tester. No screenshot/video attachment was provided in this run.

[Fullscreen] Integrate Panorama View (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN renders 360° panoramas with Three.js + expo-gl and custom shaders (src/threejs, src/pages/panorama); see docs/analyze.md §3.1, §3.2. The Flutter port needs an equivalent equirectangular 360° renderer (e.g. a panorama view package or a custom GL/OpenGL widget).

Goal

Implement the fullscreen 360° panorama viewer in Flutter: render an equirectangular panorama as an interactive sphere the user can pan/look around by dragging.

Scope

  • Fullscreen view that loads a local equirectangular image onto a sphere/projection.
  • Drag-to-look (yaw/pitch) with reasonable initial heading/fov.
  • Loading + error states; smooth performance for large images.

Out of Scope

  • Device-motion control, zoom, and connection arrows (separate Fullscreen tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • A panorama opens fullscreen and renders correctly (no seams/distortion).
  • Drag pans the view smoothly (yaw + pitch).
  • Initial heading/fov applied from panorama data where present.
  • Loading/error states handled; large images don't crash/freeze.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Open panorama fullscreen (happy path)

  1. Tap a panorama → Fullscreen.
  2. Expected: 360° image renders; can look around by dragging.

TC-2 — Rendering quality

  1. Inspect the rendered sphere.
  2. Expected: No visible seam, gross distortion, or upside-down image.

TC-3 — Initial orientation

  1. Open a panorama with a stored heading.
  2. Expected: View starts at the expected heading/fov.

TC-4 — Large image performance

  1. Open a high-resolution panorama.
  2. Expected: Loads with a progress/placeholder; pans smoothly.

TC-5 — Error handling

  1. Open a missing/corrupt image.
  2. Expected: Clear error; no crash.

TC-6 — Close/return

  1. Exit fullscreen.
  2. Expected: Returns to Tour Detail cleanly; resources released.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: opening the viewer does not modify panorama data.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: PASS — real-device mobile validation was completed with real data. No coding bug was confirmed.

[Fullscreen] Integrate Device Motion (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN uses gyro-driven viewing via expo-sensors + custom DeviceOrientationControls (src/threejs); see docs/analyze.md §3.1. Flutter port uses device sensors (gyroscope/accelerometer) to drive the panorama camera.

Goal

Implement device-motion control in the fullscreen panorama viewer: moving/rotating the phone pans the 360° view (gyro-driven look-around), with a toggle.

Scope

  • Use device orientation sensors to drive yaw/pitch in the fullscreen viewer.
  • A toggle to enable/disable motion control (fallback to drag).
  • Smooth, low-latency response; sensible calibration to current heading.

Out of Scope

  • Base panorama rendering (separate task), zoom, arrows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Enabling device motion makes the view follow phone movement.
  • Toggle switches between motion and drag control cleanly.
  • Motion is smooth (no excessive jitter/lag).
  • Disabling restores drag-only control.
  • Handles devices lacking the required sensors gracefully.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Motion control (happy path)

  1. Open fullscreen → enable Device Motion → move the phone.
  2. Expected: The view pans following the phone's orientation.

TC-2 — Toggle off

  1. Disable Device Motion.
  2. Expected: View stops following motion; drag still works.

TC-3 — Smoothness

  1. Rotate the phone steadily.
  2. Expected: Smooth tracking; no severe jitter or drift.

TC-4 — Calibration

  1. Enable motion at a given heading.
  2. Expected: View aligns sensibly with the current orientation (no jarring jump).

TC-5 — No sensors

  1. Run on a device without gyroscope (or simulate).
  2. Expected: Graceful fallback to drag; clear handling, no crash.

TC-6 — Background/return

  1. Background the app during motion, then return.
  2. Expected: Motion resumes correctly; no stuck state.

Platforms: Android + iOS (physical device needed for sensors)
Regression watch: drag control and rendering unaffected when motion is off.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED — real-device mobile validation with real data found one device-motion coding defect. All other executed task scenarios passed.

ID Method Scenario Real-device result Status
TC-1 White / Gray Box Enable Device Motion and rotate the phone Motion mode enabled and the panorama responded to device movement PASS
TC-2 Gray Box Disable Device Motion and use drag control Motion stopped and drag control continued to work PASS
TC-3 Black Box Rotate the phone steadily General motion response remained usable; see the confirmed vertical-orientation defect below FAIL — Bug
TC-4 Gray Box Enable motion from a chosen panorama heading Motion mode enabled without a disruptive initial jump PASS
TC-5 Black Box Sensor-unavailable fallback The fallback was handled safely with no application crash PASS
TC-6 Black Box Background the application during motion and return Motion resumed correctly with no stuck state or crash PASS
Regression Gray / Black Box Use fullscreen viewer with motion disabled Panorama rendering and drag interaction remained unaffected; no panorama or tour data changed PASS

Confirmed Coding Bug

Severity Actual result Expected result Impact
High After rotating the phone from down to up through one full movement and returning it to the forward-facing position, the point of view did not return to the panorama front. The bottom of the panorama was displayed instead. The point of view must track the phone orientation consistently and return near the front view when the phone returns to its original forward-facing orientation. Vertical device-motion navigation is inaccurate and disorienting; users cannot reliably look around the panorama with phone motion.

[Fullscreen] Integrate Zoom (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN supports pinch-zoom in the panorama viewer (src/components/pinch-zoom-responder); see docs/analyze.md §3.1/§3.2. Flutter port maps zoom to the viewer's field-of-view (or scale).

Goal

Implement zoom in the fullscreen panorama viewer: pinch to zoom in/out (adjusting fov/scale) within sensible bounds.

Scope

  • Pinch-to-zoom gesture adjusting the viewer fov/zoom level.
  • Min/max zoom clamping; zoom composes with drag (and device motion).
  • Optional double-tap to reset zoom.

Out of Scope

  • Base rendering, device motion, arrows (separate tasks).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Pinch gesture zooms the panorama in/out smoothly.
  • Zoom is clamped to min/max (no inversion / extreme distortion).
  • Zoom works together with panning (and motion when enabled).
  • Reset (e.g. double-tap) returns to default zoom.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

TC-1 — Pinch zoom (happy path)

  1. Open fullscreen → pinch out / in.
  2. Expected: View zooms in/out smoothly.

TC-2 — Min/max clamping

  1. Zoom to extremes.
  2. Expected: Stops at sensible bounds; no inversion or broken view.

TC-3 — Zoom + pan together

  1. Zoom in, then drag.
  2. Expected: Can pan around while zoomed.

TC-4 — Reset zoom

  1. Double-tap (or reset control).
  2. Expected: Returns to default zoom level.

TC-5 — Zoom + device motion

  1. Enable motion, then zoom.
  2. Expected: Both work together without conflict.

TC-6 — Performance

  1. Zoom on a high-resolution panorama.
  2. Expected: Remains smooth; no crash.

Platforms: Android + iOS
Regression watch: panning and rendering remain correct at all zoom levels.

QA Test Summary — 4 August 2026

Verdict: BUG CONFIRMED — real-device mobile validation with real data found one zoom-reset coding defect. All other executed task scenarios passed.

TC-2 Black Box Zoom to minimum and maximum limits Zoom remained within safe bounds; no inversion, blank view, or severe distortion was observed PASS
TC-3 Gray Box Pan while zoomed Panorama panning remained functional at zoomed levels PASS
TC-4 White / Black Box Reset zoom after changing it No reset occurred after double-tapping the panorama. The zoom slider must be opened from its menu, and double-tapping either the panorama or slider thumb did not reset the zoom. FAIL — Bug

Users must manually estimate the default zoom level and cannot reliably recover the intended initial view.

[Fullscreen] Integrate Arrow Connection (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: In the panorama viewer, directional arrows represent connections so the viewer can "walk" to a linked panorama; see docs/analyze.md §2.2, §3.3 (connections: main_id, link_id, angle).

Goal

Implement connection arrows in the fullscreen panorama viewer: render directional arrows for the current panorama's connections (positioned by angle) and navigate to the linked panorama on tap.

Scope

  • Render an arrow per connection of the current panorama, placed using the connection angle/heading.

[Listing Detail] Update Tour (Flutter Migration)

Migration context: Port of GoThru 360 Virtual Tour Maker (React Native / Expo) → Flutter.
Source reference: RN listing detail (src/pages/listings-detail) manages a published/listed tour on GoThru; see docs/analyze.md §2.6 (listings), §2.7 (publish), §3.4 (listings API apil.gothru.co), and projects fields in §3.3.

Goal

Implement "Update Tour" in Listing Detail: push edits made to a listed tour (metadata and/or panorama changes) back to GoThru so the live listing reflects the latest state.

Scope

  • Update action that sends changed listing/tour data to the GoThru API.
  • Reflect server response in local state (status, updated timestamps).
  • Progress + success/failure feedback; respect connectivity.

Out of Scope

  • Publishing to Google (separate task); activate/deactivate (separate task); discarding changes (separate task).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Update sends the current changes to GoThru and confirms success.
  • Local state reflects the updated server status after success.
  • Requires connectivity; clear error + retry on failure (no silent failure).
  • Works with the signed-in session token; labels via i18n.

🧪 Test Scenarios (for QA)

  1. Open a listing → make a change → Update Tour.

  1. Attempt update offline.
  2. Expected: Clear "no internet" message; update not started.

  1. Simulate a server error, then retry.
  2. Expected: Error surfaced; retry completes successfully.

  1. Update, relaunch, reopen the listing.
  2. Expected: Updated state persists/refetches consistently.

  1. Switch language.
  2. Expected: Labels/status/errors translated.
